object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who books appointments at the clinic

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments. Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient, and a patient can have many appointments.
Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A physician who sees patients at the clinic

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments.
Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled meeting between a patient and a doctor

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments.
Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: Exam Room
object_types.definition: A physical room in the clinic used for exams

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: A medical specialty area a doctor practices in, e.g. cardiology or general practice

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: Appointment Date
object_types.definition: The calendar date on which an appointment occurs

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot

object_types.name: Time Slot
object_types.definition: A fixed time slot for an appointment, e.g. 09:00 or 09:30

source_references.excerpt: we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30

object_types.name: Appointment Status
object_types.definition: The current state of an appointment

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.

object_types.name: Visit Reason
object_types.definition: The reason a patient gives for the visit when booking an appointment

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking

object_types.name: Follow-up Note
object_types.definition: A note attached by the doctor after a visit

source_references.excerpt: after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: The relationship between 'primary doctor' and the doctor seen in a given appointment is stated to be separate/independent, but it's unclear whether any subset or exclusion constraint should hold between them (e.g., can the doctor seen in an appointment differ from the primary doctor, or is it common/expected they coincide?). The transcript only clarifies they are conceptually distinct facts, not any constraint between them.
